desc:
The array nums has an even length 2n. Divide its elements (by position) into two groups of exactly n elements each. Return the smallest possible value of |sum of group 1 - sum of group 2|.

Values may be negative. For example, nums = [3, 9, 7, 3] gives 2 (groups {3, 9} and {7, 3} sum to 12 and 10), and nums = [-36, 36] gives 72 because each group must hold exactly one element.
hints: Choosing which n of the 2n elements form group 1 means looking at C(2n, n) subsets, about 40 million for 2n = 28. That is too many to test one by one in a slow language.
Cut the array into a left half and a right half of n elements each. Group 1 takes k elements from the left half and n - k from the right half, for some k between 0 and n.

For each k, list the sums of all k-element subsets of the left half and of all (n-k)-element subsets of the right half. Sort one list and, for each sum in the other list, binary search for the partner that brings group 1's total closest to half of the grand total.
editorial: Let total be the sum of all elements and A the sum of group 1. The difference is |total - 2A|, so we want A as close to total / 2 as possible among all selections of exactly n elements.

Meet in the middle. Split the array into halves L and R of n elements. Enumerate all 2n subsets of each half (with n ≤ 14 that is 16,384) with their sums, grouped by subset size. Group 1 takes a subset of size k from L and a subset of size n - k from R, so for each k we combine the size-k sums of L with the size-(n-k) sums of R.

For a fixed left sum l, we want a right sum r minimising |total - 2l - 2r|. Sort the right sums once per k, binary search for the value nearest to (total - 2l) / 2 and inspect its neighbours. The total work is about 2 · 2n for enumeration plus 2n binary searches, i.e. O(2n · n), instead of C(2n, n).
solution:
from bisect import bisect_left


def closestEqualSizeSplit(nums):
    n = len(nums) // 2
    total = sum(nums)
    left = nums[:n]
    right = nums[n:]

    def by_size(a):
        m = len(a)
        sums = [0] * (1 << m)
        cnt = [0] * (1 << m)
        groups = [[] for _ in range(m + 1)]
        groups[0].append(0)
        for mask in range(1, 1 << m):
            low = mask & -mask
            rest = mask ^ low
            sums[mask] = sums[rest] + a[low.bit_length() - 1]
            cnt[mask] = cnt[rest] + 1
            groups[cnt[mask]].append(sums[mask])
        return groups

    gl = by_size(left)
    gr = by_size(right)
    best = float('inf')
    for k in range(n + 1):
        rs = sorted(gr[n - k])
        for l in gl[k]:
            target = total - 2 * l
            idx = bisect_left(rs, target // 2)
            for q in (idx - 1, idx, idx + 1):
                if 0 <= q < len(rs):
                    d = abs(target - 2 * rs[q])
                    if d < best:
                        best = d
    return best
